text: Supermarket checkout. Cart full, you want to leave. Eye the lines, craving speed.
"10 items or less!" The express lane. You slide in, confident you've outsmarted the system, for a quick escape.
But familiar dread. Your express lane isn't moving. It feels slower than others. Did you pick the worst one, again?
The invisible truth: fewer items seems faster, but each transaction has fixed overhead – scanning, payment, bagging. More people choose this lane, because everyone thinks like you.
This lane often processes more *transactions* per hour. Your memory, biased by frustration, reinforces the feeling you pick the slow line.
Tomorrow, you’ll return. Now, you know the hidden rule. You see the total flow, not just item count. The express lane won't fool you again.
